1
Haan Woh Hain Mujtaba Haan Woh Hain Mujtaba.
Jin Se Hoi Hai Sorah-e-Kausar Ki Ibtida.
Chalne Se Tha Youn Lagta Muhammad Hain Chal Rahe.
Maidaan Mein Tha Youn Lagta Ali Hain Khare Hoye.
Lagte Hain Mujh Ko Mazhar-e-Aousaf-e-Kibriya.
Raziq Khuda Hai Sab Ka Koi Iss Mein Shak Nahi.
Hai Sadqa Mujtaba Ka Mujhe Yeh Bhi Hai Yaqeen.
Dastar Khuwaan Jis Ka Aaj Bhi Bichta Hai Har Jagah.
Uthti Jo Taig Oss Ki Koi Bachta Phir Kahan.
Deen-e-Khuda Ki Khatir Kya Sab Pe Yeh Ayyan.
Jis Ne Ameer-e-Sham Ko Qalam Se Hara Diya.
Ik Dushman-e-Ali Tha Darbar Mein Khara.
Mula Hasan Ke Jad Ko Kaha Os Ne Kuch Bura.
Oss Mard Ko Tha Jis Ne Aurat Bana Diya.
Khairat Hai Yeh Yousufi Qirtas Pe Tere.
Ashar Warna Kaise Hasan Ke Hain Yeh Likhte.
Har Ik Faqeer Ke Liye Hai Jis Ka Dar Khula.

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/haan-woh-hain-mujtaba-haan-woh-hain-mujtaba-tajpoints-34f6f22ef5eefdd20186.md')
def parts(s):
    _, meta, body = s.split('---\\n', 2)
    return meta, body.strip().splitlines()
old = parts(subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{p}'], text=True))[1]
meta, body = parts(p.read_text())
roman = meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1].splitlines()
assert all(line.startswith('  ') for line in roman)
assert [line.strip().casefold() for line in roman] == [line.rstrip('.').casefold() for line in old]
assert body[0] == '۱' and len(body) == len(roman) == 18
assert all(any('\\u0600' <= c <= '\\u06ff' for c in line) for line in body[1:])
assert '\\u200c' not in ''.join(body)
print('Verified 17 aligned verses and unchanged Roman wording.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 17 verses in Urdu script, preserving the original order and single stanza. Moved the Roman wording into `romanLyrics`, updated the Urdu title and right-to-left direction, and removed the `noUrdu` tag. Verified that both versions contain 17 verse lines.

I read the ambiguous Roman “Jad” as جد, meaning “ancestor,” and “Kya” as کیا, meaning “made” in “made evident.”
